title: Han Xin Repays the Washerwoman
text:
As a young man in Huaiyin, in the late 3rd century BC, Han Xin was poor, idle and widely despised. He could not earn a living and often lived off other people. Sima Qian records that he went fishing under the city walls, where some old women were washing silk floss in the river. One of them saw he was starving and shared her food with him every day for several weeks until the washing was done.

Han Xin was delighted and promised he would repay her richly one day. She was angry. A grown man who could not feed himself, she said: she had fed him out of pity, not in hope of any reward.

Years later Han Xin had become one of the greatest generals in Chinese history, the man who won the wars that founded the Han dynasty. He was made King of Chu, ruling his home region. When he returned, he sought out the old washerwoman and gave her a thousand pieces of gold.
lesson: Remember who helped you when you had nothing and could offer nothing back. Repaying old kindness when you are able is one of the surest marks of character.
source: Sima Qian, Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), chapter 92, Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin
